findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.citation_text:
2-301.14 
Observed employee change gloves without hand washing. PIC was made aware and education conducted. Ensure that all employees who handle food wash their hands properly after and before doning gloves. 

When to Wash. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms as specified under § 2-301.12 immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including working with exposed FOOD, clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and: (G) Before donning gloves to initiate a task that involves working with FOOD

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
findings.citation_text:
6-301.12 
Observed paper towel dispenser to have ran out at the hand sink in the dish machine area. PIC was informed and corrected. Make sure all hand washing sinks are provided with paper towels at all times.

Hand Drying Provision. Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels; (B) A continuous towel system that supplies the user with a clean towel; or (C) A heated-air hand drying device; or (D) A hand drying device that employs an air-knife system that delivers high velocity, pressurized air at ambient temperatures.

findings.title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated.
findings.citation_text:
3-101.11 
Observed some rotten potatoes in an open cardboard box in the back room. PIC was informed and instructed to throw away. Make sure that all food shall be safe, unadulterated and honestly presented. The potatoes were discarded to correct. 

Safe, Unadulterated, and Honestly Presented. FOOD shall be safe, unADULTERATED, and, as specified under § 3-601.12, honestly presented.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.citation_text:
4-602.11(A) 
(1) Multiple pans, utensils and knives stored throughout the facility were observed with contaminants remaining after cleaning and in storage. (2) Can opener blade observed to be soiled with residue. The PIC was shown and the items moved back to dish for re-cleaning. It is highly suggested that education is conducted in house for dish washers to ensure that food contact items are completely cleaned prior to storage and use. Ensure that all dishes are completely cleaned prior to storage and future use. 

Equipment Food-Contact Surfaces and Utensils. (A) Equipment food-contact surfaces and utensils shall be cleaned: (5) At any time during the operation when contamination may have occurred.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.citation_text:
6-501.16 Observed mops stored with the heads pooled up on the floor in the mop sink. PIC was made aware and corrected during the inspection. Ensure that mop heads must be stored in a manner that allows them to air dry and prevents contamination. 

Drying Mops. After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to air-dry without soiling walls, EQUIPMENT, or supplies.

findings.title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used.
findings.citation_text:
6-403.11(B) 
Observed personal drinks(soda glass, water bottles) in multiple area in the facility with food prep and storage areas (kitchen and walk in cooler). PIC was made aware and educated. Make sure personal drinks are stored in designated areas only to prevent potential contamination.

Designated Areas. (B) Lockers or other suitable facilities shall be located in a designated room or area where contamination of FOOD, EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, LINENS, and SINGLESERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES can not occur.

findings.title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored and used.
findings.citation_text:
7-201.11 Separation. Poisonous or toxic materials shall be stored so they can not contaminate food, equipment, utensils, linens, and single-service and single-use articles by: (B) Locating the POISONOUS OR TOXIC MATERIALS in an area that is not above FOOD, EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE or SINGLE-USE ARTICLES.

An aerosol can of glass cleaner was observed on a shelf over cleaned and stored dishes between the walk-ins. The PIC was shown and removed the can to correct the immediate violation. Ensure that all chemicals not intended for direct contact to food contact surfaces are stored so that they do not pose a potential source of contamination to foods or food contact surfaces.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
findings.citation_text:
2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM). (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

The PIC during this inspection did not have a CFPM and did not know of any others in the area that did. The normal person that does have one was off that day. Ensure that there are enough CFPM’s available to cover all shifts.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.citation_text:
2-301.12(B) Cleaning Procedure. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use the following cleaning procedure in the order stated to clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms, including surrogate prosthetic devices for hands and arms: (5) Immediately follow the cleaning procedure with thorough drying using a method as specified under § 6-301.12.

An employee was observed to wash their hands and use their bare hands to turn off the faucet. Education was conducted and the PIC is instructed to review hand washing with all employees. Ensure that the hand washing procedure in the facility does not allow for recontaminating the hands at the end of the process.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.citation_text:
2-301.14 When to Wash. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms as specified under § 2-301.12 immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including working with exposed FOOD, clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and: (H) Before donning gloves to initiate a task that involves working with FOOD.

An employee was observed to don gloves without hand washing. The PIC was consulted and instructed to review when to wash hands with all employees. Ensure that hand washing takes place before donning gloves.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.citation_text:
4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11.

The only sani bucket observed in the kitchen during the inspection did not register on either the inspector's or facility’s test strips. The PIC was consulted and stated that the bucket was made around 11 in the morning. The bucket was remade to correct concentration during the inspection. Ensure that the sanitizers are refreshed often enough so that they are maintained at effective concentrations at all times.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
findings.citation_text:
3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY (TCS) FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less. 

TCS foods in the prep cooler are observed with internal temperatures ranging from 46F-50F. The ambient air temperature is also observed at 50F. The PIC was consulted and the situation investigated. TCS items were discarded to correct the immediate violation and include sliced ham, chicken, shrimp, goat cheese, mozzarella cheese and lettuce. Sliced tomatoes and pre-made/packaged hard boiled eggs were moved to the adjacent standing cooler as they had just been prepared. Refer to line item #33 for the follow up on cooler functionality.

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control.
findings.citation_text:
4-301.11 Cooling, Heating, and Holding Capacities. EQUIPMENT for cooling and heating FOOD, and holding cold and hot FOOD, shall be sufficient in number and capacity to provide FOOD temperatures as specified under Chapter 3. 

The prep cooler in the kitchen is not correctly holding food temperatures during this inspection. The cooler is being temporarily taken out of service as a short term solution and maintenance shall be conducted to repair/ adjust. Follow up in ten days to ensure that the maintinance is conducted and effective.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
findings.citation_text:
4-303.11(B) Cleaning Agents and Sanitizers, Availability. (B) Except for those that are generated on-site at the time of use, chemical SANITIZERS that are used to sanitize EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS as specified under Part 4-7, shall be provided and available for use during all hours of operation.

On arrival and throughout the walk through a sanitizer was not observed ready for use in the kitchen. The PIC was asked about this and made a new bucket for the kitchen. Food preparation was taking place at all times during this inspection. Ensure that there are sanitizers ready for use at all times that foods are being handled and/or prepared.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.citation_text:
4-602.11(A) Equipment Food-Contact Surfaces and Utensils. (A) Equipment food-contact surfaces and utensils shall be cleaned: (5) At any time during the operation when contamination may have occurred.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
5-205.11: (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. 

On arrival the hand sink in the dish room is blocked by a can and a stand. The PIC was consulted and moved the items to correct. Ensure that the hand sinks are maintained accessible at all times to promote regular and consistent hand washing.

findings.title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated
findings.comment:
3-202.15: FOOD packages shall be in good condition and protect the integrity of the contents so that the FOOD is not exposed to ADULTERATION or potential contaminants. 

Multiple cans in the dry storage area are observed with significant dents in the top and bottom seams. The PIC was consulted and educated about the related concerns and the cans were separated out for credit to correct. Ensure that any dented/damaged cans are separated out to ensure that they are not used at this facility.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria.

The sani bucket in the kitchen did not produce a color change on the inspector’s test strips. The dispenser was checked and produced effective concentrations after the hose was placed into the concentrate more fully. A new bucket was made to correct the immediate violation.

findings.title: Charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties
findings.comment:
The PERSON IN CHARGE shall: (K) proper sanitizing.

The dish machine is not properly sanitizing dishes at the time of this inspection (refer to line item #16). A temporary measure is in place to allow for continued service while the machine is having maintenance conducted. This is a follow up for 10 days to ensure that the repair is made.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.comment:
2-102.12: (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM. 

A CFPM was not available during this inspection in this facility. The current kitchen manager is on an extended medical leave. CFPM courses were discussed and attached to the email report for this facility. Ensure that there is a CFPM present in the facility at all times that food handling operations are taking place.

findings.title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated
findings.comment:
3-202.15: FOOD packages shall be in good condition and protect the integrity of the contents so that the FOOD is not exposed to ADULTERATION or potential contaminants. 

Multiple cans in the dry storage area are observed with significant dents in the top and bottom seams. The PIC was consulted and educated about the related concerns and the cans were separated out for credit to correct. Ensure that any dented/damaged cans are put into rotation for use at this facility.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-703.11: After cleaning, FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES shall be SANITIZED in: (A) manual hot water operations. (B) mechanical hot water operations. (C) Chemical manual or mechanical operations. Contact times shall be consistent with those on EPA-registered label.

The dish machine in the kitchen did not register 160F or higher on either the inspector’s or facility’s maximum registering thermometers. The inspector also attempted color changing dots that did not register a change. The machine was ran multiple times in an attempt to reach needed temperature thresholds without success. The facility will use the three part sink temporarily for the sanitize step to correct. Refer to line item #1 for the follow up on the machine functionality.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-601.11: (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. 

The blade of the can opener is heavily soiled during this inspection. The situation was discussed with the PIC and the opener moved to dish for cleaning to correct. Ensure that the food contact surfaces are maintained clean at all times between uses.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
6-301.12: Each HANDWASHING SINK shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels; (B) A continuous towel system that supplies the user with a clean towel; (C) A heated-air hand drying device; (D) A hand drying device that employs an air-knife system that delivers high velocity, pressurized air at ambient temperatures. 

The hand sink in the dish area is observed without paper towels during this inspection. Paper towels were supplied during this inspection to correct. Ensure that all hand sinks are properly supplied at all times to promote correct hand washing.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria.

The sani bucket in the food prep area would not produce a color change on the inspector’s test strips. Sanitizer used is quaternary ammonia based. The bucket was remade during the inspection to correct.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.comment:
4-302.13: (B) In hot water mechanical WAREWASHING operations, an irreversible registering temperature indicator shall be provided and readily accessible for measuring the UTENSIL surface temperature. [Pf]

Facility does not have irreversible registering temperature indicator available to monitor dish machine rinse temperature. Provide supplies to monitor dish machine rinse temperature (maximum registering thermometer or heat sensitive stickers/strips). Follow up scheduled for two weeks.

findings.title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated
findings.comment:
3-202.15: FOOD packages shall be in good condition and protect the integrity of the contents so that the FOOD is not exposed to ADULTERATION or potential contaminants. 

Multiple cans in the dry storage room are observed with significant dents in the upper/lower seams. Education was conducted with the PIC and the observed cans set aside for credit/replacement.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-602.11: (A) FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES shall be cleaned before each use, each time there is a change in work, between uses of raw FOODS to RTE FOODS, before using FOOD TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE, and when contamination has occurred. (C) Cleaned at least every 4 hours. 

The blade of the can opener is observed soiled during this inspection. It was moved to dish for cleaning/sanitizing to correct.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-601.11: (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. 

Tongs stored in the back room appear soiled with grease/oil. They do not seem to have been fully cleaned when ran through dish. PIC was consulted and instructed to ensure that dish washers ensure all dishes are fully cleaned prior to storage. The tongs were moved back to dish for cleaning.

findings.title: Single-use/single-service articles: properly stored and used
findings.comment:
4-903.11: (A) clean EQUIPMENT and clean ARTICLES shall be stored in clean, dry location where they are not exposed to contamination and at least 6 inches above the floor. (C) SINGLE-USE ARTICLES shall be kept in original PACKAGE or stored in manner to protect it against contamination. 

A plastic container of plastic spoons and forks is observed with the eating ends intermixed with the handles as well as packets of ketchup, mustard and sugar. Per the PIC the container is sent out with the service trays for residents. The food contact surfaces should be protected form contamination. A new system will need to be devised prior to the next routine inspection.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.comment:
4-303.11: (B) Chemical SANITIZERS shall be provided and available during all hours of operation. 

Throughout the inspection no sanitizers were available for use in the kitchen areas. A bucket was provided during the inspection to correct the violation.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
4-601.11: (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris. 

The outside of a container of cocktail sauce to the left as you enter the walk in cooler has multiple mold colonies apparent on the lid and upper sections. PIC was consulted and the container discarded during the inspection to correct the violation.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-201.11: Except as specified under § 6-201.14 and except for antislip floor coverings or applications that may be used for safety reasons, floors, floor coverings, walls, wall coverings, and ceilings shall be designed, constructed, and installed so they are SMOOTH and EASILY CLEANABLE.

Caulk around the dish machine in the kitchen observed to be cracked or pulling away. Repair caulking.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
2-301.12: (A) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of arms for at least 20 seconds. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use proper procedure (C) To prevent recontamination, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use barrier to operate faucet handles. (D) Automatic handwashing facility may be used if APPROVED. 

A food employee was observed to wash their hands and then use their bare hand to turn off the faucet prior to attempting to get a paper towel. Education was conducted to correct.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
6-301.11: Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of 2 adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with a supply of hand cleaning liquid, powder, or bar soap. 

The hand sink next to the cooking area is observed with hand sanitizer for use. PIC was notified and switched the container to hand soup during the inspection.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
6-301.12: Each HANDWASHING SINK shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels; (B) A continuous towel system that supplies the user with a clean towel; (C) A heated-air hand drying device; (D) A hand drying device that employs an air-knife system that delivers high velocity, pressurized air at ambient temperatures. 

The hand sink next to the grills has a paper towel dispenser that is out of batteries (per the PIC) and is not functioning off of the sensor at this time. PIC indicated that the batteries should be replaced soon (they are waiting on the maintenance person). At this time PIC indicated that they were using their elbows to open the machine and get out paper towels as needed, but this does not appear to be an effective method. Inspector suggested leaving the dispenser open until it can be brought back into easy use.

findings.title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used
findings.comment:
7-102.11: Working containers used for storing POISONOUS OR TOXIC MATERIALS such as cleaners and SANITIZERS taken from bulk supplies shall be clearly and individually identified with the common name of the material. 

A spray bottle with a blue/green liquid is observed in the kitchen without a label indicating what chemical is inside. PIC smelled the bottle and believes that the chemical is an air freshener of some kind. The bottle was removed from the kitchen to correct the immediate violation and the PIC is aware that all chemicals in the prep areas need labels.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
Employee washed hands, then turned the faucet off without using a barrier to prevent recontamination of hands. CORRECTED- Discussed with PIC and employee. Employee re-washed hands.
2-301.12 (C) TO avoid recontaminating their hands or surrogate prosthetic devices, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use disposable paper towels or similar clean barriers when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a HANDWASHING SINK or the handle of a restroom door. (P)

Employee moved from handling dirty to clean dishes without washing hands in between. CORRECTED- Discussed with PIC. Provided education.
findings.citation_text: 2-301.14 FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms as specified under § 2-301.12 immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including working with exposed FOOD, clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and (E) After handling soiled EQUIPMENT or UTENSILS. (P)

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment: Handwashing sink in the memory care kitchen is not labeled with a handwashing sign. CORRECTED- Inspector provided handwashing sign to be posted near the memory care kitchen handwashing sink.
findings.citation_text: 6-301.14 A sign or poster that notifies FOOD EMPLOYEES to wash their hands shall be provided at all HANDWASHING SINKS used by FOOD EMPLOYEES and shall be clearly visible to FOOD EMPLOYEES. (C)

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment: Can opener is soiled with food debris. Wash, rinse, and sanitize after each use, or every 4 hours during continuous use. CORRECTED- Can opener was removed to be washed, rinsed, and sanitized.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11 (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. (Pf)

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment: Date of 2/12 marked on chocolate pudding in the walk-in cooler exceeds the time limit. Date of 2/3 marked on sliced onions in the walk-in cooler. CORRECTED- Out of date foods were voluntarily discarded.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.17 Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours must be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the food must be consumed on the premises, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 41°F or less for a maximum of 7 days.

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display
findings.comment: Sugar is not protected from contamination during storage-- lid is left open and contamination is observed in the food. Food shall be protected from contamination.
findings.citation_text: 3-305.11 (A) Except as specified in ¶¶ (B) and (C) of this section, FOOD shall be protected from contamination by storing the FOOD: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where it is not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor. (C)

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
findings.comment: In-use wiping cloths are not stored properly. Cloths used for wiping spills shall be maintained dry. Cloths used to wipe surfaces and equipment shall be held in proper sanitizer solution. CORRECTED- Cloth was removed to be laundered. Ensure wiping cloths are stored dry, or held in sanitizing solution.
findings.citation_text: 3-304.14 (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and other EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be: (1) Held between uses in a chemical sanitizer solution at a concentration specified under § 4-501.114. (C)

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment: A sign or poster that notifies food employees to wash their hands is not provided at the buffet handwashing sink. Also no signage posted at the handwashing sink in the memory care kitchen. Provide a clearly visible handwashing sign at each hand sink. CORRECTED- Inspector provided "Proper Handwashing" signs to be posted at the memory care kitchen handwashing sink.
findings.citation_text: 6-301.14 A sign or poster that notifies FOOD EMPLOYEES to wash their hands shall be provided at all HANDWASHING SINKS used by FOOD EMPLOYEES and shall be clearly visible to FOOD EMPLOYEES. (C)

findings.title: Thermometers provided & accurate
findings.comment: A thermometer is not provided in the vertical cooler. Cold/Hot holding equipment used for Time/Temperature Control for Safety food shall have at least one thermometer in an easily viewed location. CORRECTED- PIC placed a new thermometer in the cooler.
findings.citation_text: 4-204.112 (A) In a mechanically refrigerated or hot FOOD storage unit, the sensor of a TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE shall be located to measure the air temperature or a simulated product temperature in the warmest part of a mechanically refrigerated unit and in the coolest part of a hot FOOD storage unit. (C)

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment: Observed carts blocking the handwashing sinks in the dish area and back prep room. Also observed a carafe in the back prep room handwashing sink. CORRECTED- Carts were relocated and carafe was removed. Discussed with PIC and provided education. Ensure handwashing sinks are always easily accessible to allow frequent handwashing.
findings.citation_text: 5-205.11 (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (Pf)

findings.title: Utensils, equipment & linens: properly stored, dried, & handled
findings.comment: Observed forks in the back prep room stored with the eating ends up. Store utensils inverted to prevent contamination during storage and handling. CORRECTED- Utensils were rearranged to be stored inverted.
findings.citation_text: 4-903.11 (B) Clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS shall be stored as specified under ¶ (A) of this section and shall be stored (2) Covered or inverted. (C)

findings.title: Single-use/single-service articles: properly stored and used
findings.comment: Observed single-use straws stored under the buffet counter sink. Store single service utensils where they are protected from contamination. CORRECTED- Straws were moved to another cabinet.
findings.citation_text: 4-903.11 (A) Except as specified in ¶ (D) of this section, cleaned EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, laundered LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES shall be stored: (1) In a clean, dry location; and (2) Where they are not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination. (C)
